title: streaming(lifecycle): robust client-cancel, disconnect handling, reconnect/resume, and server timeout heuristics
author: Priya Shah
description: Motivation: streaming endpoints have been a source of intermittent failures for long-running chat sessions when clients cancel, disconnect mid-stream, or attempt reconnect/resume. This PR centralizes lifecycle controls for server-side streaming paths to make client cancel a first-class signal, improve disconnect handling, provide a reconnect/resume mechanism compatible with OpenAI-style clients, and introduce server-side timeout heuristics to avoid runaway resources. Summary: - Add explicit client-cancel wire-level handling so servers can eagerly free per-request state and KV cache slots. - Track transport lifecycle (connected, disconnected, reconnected) and expose resume tokens for clients to continue partial streams within a time window. - Implement server-side idle and resume timeouts with adaptive heuristics based on model max_length and current KV memory pressure. - Backfill OpenAI-compatibility layer to honor cancel/disconnect events and map reconnect/resume semantics to existing session store. Checklist: 1) tests covering client cancel and server free paths 2) reconnect/resume e2e with OpenAI-compatible SDKs 3) metrics/tracing added for lifecycle transitions 4) feature gated behind runtime flag for safe rollout. Changeset overview (single-string): Commits implement a new StreamingLifecycle controller, add ResumeToken generation and validation, introduce lifecycle state transitions persisted to session-store, add server timeout heuristics (idle_timeout_ms, max_resume_window_ms) and knobs on per-route config, and wire OpenAI compatibility mapping for cancel/resume events. Files changed include small runtime wiring, session-store schema migration, a few unit and integration tests, and doc updates. Backwards compatibility: default behavior unchanged unless runtime flag enabled; OpenAI compatibility is opt-in per route. Rollout plan: enable flag for internal beta, run dogfooding with dedicated capacity, monitor lifecycle metrics, then flip on for hosted traffic with gradual rollout.

release_notes: Server: streaming lifecycle controls: clients can now send explicit cancel and reconnect/resume flows. Adds ResumeTokens and server-side idle/resume timeouts. Opt-in via runtime flag 'streaming.lifecycle_v1'. Backwards compatible by default. Monitor metrics: stream.lifecycle.transitions, stream.resume_tokens.*.
testing_summary: Unit tests (streaming lifecycle state transitions, token edge cases) and integration tests (client cancel, abrupt disconnect, reconnect/resume with OpenAI-compatible client) added. CI runs passed. Manual dogfood on dedicated capacity confirmed resource cleanup within 1s of client-cancel, and resume succeeded within configured window for valid tokens.
deploy_notes: Feature gated behind runtime flag; requires session-store migration (non-blocking). Rollout: internal beta -> 10% hosted -> 100% once metrics stable. Operators: watch stream.idle_timeout_triggers and stream.resume_token_miss_rate.
notes_for_oncall: If you see elevated stream.resume_token_miss_rate, it usually means session GC or migration lag; safe fallback is to instruct client to re-issue request (full new session). If memory pressure spikes, the heuristics will shorten resume window; consider increasing capacity for workloads needing long resume windows.
examples: OpenAI-compat client: send 'CANCEL' event -> server emits 'cancelled' lifecycle transition and frees KV slots
Reconnect flow: client reconnects with ResumeToken header 'x-resume-token' -> server validates token and emits 'resumed' or returns 410 if expired
Timeout behavior: server will close session after idle_timeout_ms and refuse resume after max_resume_window_ms
